articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino's Man United moment has arrived. Is he ready?
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino faces the sizable challenge of restoring Man United to their former glory. Can he succeed where Michael Carrick, Ruben Amorim and others failed?
articles.headlineJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノにマンチェスター・ユナイテッドを率いる時が来た。彼は準備ができているか？
articles.descriptionJa: ポチェッティーノは、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドに往時の栄光を取り戻させるという大きな課題に直面している。マイケル・キャリックやルーベン・アモリムらが成し遂げられなかったことを、彼は実現できるだろうか。
articles.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- When Manchester United unveiled their new and improved Carrington training base in August 2025, it included a revamped media theater. In the 15 months since, Ruben Amorim, Darren Fletcher and Michael Carrick have sat in the hot seat for news conferences.

On Friday, Mauricio Pochettino became the fourth occupant this year, a testament to the turmoil that has continued to engulf Old Trafford in the 13 years since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement. Like the others before him, United's new head coach is simultaneously tasked with steadying the ship after the latest rocky spell and also -- eventually -- returning the club to the top of English football.

It's a sizable challenge, and Pochettino is aware that he doesn't have a moment to waste. He began his first meeting with reporters on Friday with an apology for being late, explaining that he wanted to squeeze in as much time as possible on the training pitch ahead of his first game against Liverpool on Sunday.

After arriving in Manchester on Wednesday afternoon, he was driven straight to the training ground from the airport. Finally finished with meetings and media duties at around 7 p.m., he went to his office to continue working rather than heading for his hotel.

On Thursday, he took charge of his first training session -- with footage later appearing online thanks to an unauthorized drone flight -- and held individual meetings with players that lasted more than three hours.

He revealed he is surviving on "three or four hours" of sleep a night. It's unlikely to improve anytime soon.

After the trip at Anfield, United face six games in 19 days. It's a packed schedule for any head coach, but especially for one who has been parachuted into a job midseason with a team rooted in the relegation zone with just one league win all season.

"I think always it's tough, even if you arrive in summer," Pochettino said. "Sometimes you arrive in summer, but you don't have time to build the squad. Sometimes you arrive in the middle and maybe players, you know, need something that you can provide."

Pochettino's to-do list

Pochettino's first job is to repair the players' confidence. In his first interview with club media Thursday, he spoke about the squad rediscovering the feeling of winning matches.

Questions about titles and trophies are never far away at United, but Pochettino is inheriting a team that is 18th in the Premier League table and facing the once-unthinkable prospect of a first relegation since 1974.

"It's normal when you don't win games, the confidence starts going down, going down, going down," he said. "I think the players need to feel something from us, like always happens with a new coaching staff, that you really believe and you really trust, and then you need to show that you know what you are doing. That is the important thing."

articles.headline: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
articles.description: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
articles.headlineJa: ジェシー・ベイツ3世をトレードに出したが、ファルコンズは依然として勝利が目標だと強調
articles.descriptionJa: アトランタは、ジェシー・ベイツ3世のトレードがチームに誤ったメッセージを送ることにならないよう配慮した。
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.

That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings. Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

"I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days -- like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

"We believe the return gives us a meaningful opportunity to strengthen this roster over time," a team source said. "That does not mean Jessie stopped being an outstanding player. We are giving up something valuable and we understand that."

On the other hand, the Falcons are in one of the most unique positions in the NFL. Their record is ugly, but they are a half-game out of first place in a weak NFC South. All four teams in the division are sitting at three wins apiece. Atlanta finishes its season playing its NFC South rivals back-to-back-to-back.

So, there was also an argument for standing pat and making a good-faith run at the playoffs, where the Falcons have not been since 2017. Only the New York Jets have a longer drought.

"We're still in it," quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said. "... We're so close in a lot of areas and I feel like in this organization we view that a lot. We use that a lot. We are so close.

"I truly believe we have the team and the guys that's going to rally and flip the script because we got a lot of guys that care. Obviously, I feel like matchup wise, I feel like our team is one of the top teams in the league."

We kick things off in the Premier League, where Enzo Maresca's Manchester City look to snap a three-game league losing streak when they host Fulham.

Later, we have a full slate of matches happening simultaneously such as Chelsea taking on Leeds United, while Tottenham Hotspur welcome Ipswich Town. Finally, we have our match of the day as Newcastle United host league leaders and defending champions Arsenal.

articles.headline: In Mexico City, 49ers' Fred Warner can represent his heritage and boost DPOY case
articles.description: Warner will represent his heritage again Sunday in Mexico City. This time while in the middle of the best Defensive Player of the Year campaign of his career.
articles.headlineJa: メキシコシティで、49ersのフレッド・ウォーナーが自身のルーツを体現し、DPOY受賞への期待を高める
articles.descriptionJa: ウォーナーは日曜日にメキシコシティで再び自身のルーツを代表してプレーする。今回は、キャリア最高の最優秀守備選手賞（DPOY）争いの真っ只中でのこととなる。
articles.body:
MEXICO CITY -- Taken four years ago to the day, the photo still follows San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner just about anywhere he goes.

It was a brisk Mexico City night in 2022 when Warner -- clad in his white No. 54 jersey, gold pants and gold helmet -- burst out of the tunnel waving the red, white and green Mexican flag that represents a significant part of his heritage. The Niners were technically the visiting team against the Cardinals. But as the roar of the crowd enveloped him, Warner felt instantly at home.

Since that game, he has come across the image everywhere from autograph lines -- where fans hand him copies to sign -- to his childhood home, where his mother, Laura, keeps a blown-up print. For a player building a Hall of Fame résumé, that pregame sprint remains a defining memory.

His reaction every time he sees it? Goosebumps.

"I don't think I understood the magnitude of the moment," Warner told ESPN on Thursday, his 30th birthday. "Being in Mexico in front of the fans, really representing them and representing that part of me and my family was bigger than I even thought."

Watching from her home in San Diego in 2022, Laura Warner saw her son's arrival with the flag in hand as the ultimate public tribute to the roots her late father passed down to their family.

"I just got chills because it was just, to me, a big moment," Laura Warner said. "Because he was representing that heritage of our family in front of everyone."

Born Federico Anthony Warner on Nov. 19, 1996, in San Marcos, California, the ninth-year linebacker leads the 49ers back to Mexico City for a Sunday night showdown against the Minnesota Vikings (8:20 p.m. ET, NBC) in a game with major implications for the NFC's No. 1 seed. He describes his 2022 trip here as "electric." This time, he carries the weight of a historic pursuit -- becoming the fourth off-ball linebacker in NFL history to win Defensive Player of the Year -- along with the pride of his family's history.

Juan Quiroz, Warner's grandfather, was born in the small village of Arandas in Jalisco, Mexico, the oldest boy in a family of 11. He moved to the Los Angeles area at 16, where he met his future wife, Doris Quiroz. They married and had three children, including Laura.

Juan died in a car accident when Laura was only 7. So Fred, who has Mexican and French-Canadian roots on his mother's side and Panamanian and African American heritage from his father, never had the chance to meet his grandfather.

Yet Juan's influence lived on through the Spanish spoken and the Mexican food shared inside Warner's childhood home. He can still rattle off his favorite staples, from his grandmother's eggs and tortillas every morning to wet burritos and carne asada tacos for dinner -- traditions that Warner said made his Mexican background "a big part of our upbringing."

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs that could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Eagles pull off an upset over the Steelers? Is 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey in for a big receiving day against the Vikings? Does Titans quarterback Cam Ward have fantasy potential against the Cowboys? Will we see another touchdown for wide receiver Josh Downs in a Chiefs uniform?

Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Philadelphia Eagles +4.5 (+180 moneyline) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers

Quarterback Aaron Rodgers hasn't given much reason to trust Pittsburgh laying points on the road Sunday. Philadelphia's specialty is playing more man coverage and sending extra rushers, both of which have bothered Rodgers in 2026. Plus, defensive tackle Jalen Carter can attack an offensive line that just lost guard Mason McCormick (ankle).

Eagles backup QB Joe Milton taking sacks is the main concern for their offense, but he can still get positive yards as a scrambler. With wide receiver DeVonta Smith potentially returning from a hamstring injury, the Eagles have enough to win this by a field goal.

Minnesota's defense remains the strength in this Sunday night matchup. Coordinator Brian Flores brings pressure from different places, and 49ers QB Brock Purdy took five sacks against Dallas in Week 10. The Vikings have also been excellent at forcing field goals near the end zone.

Quarterback Kirk Cousins faces a tough matchup himself in his second start for Minnesota, but he gives it a more reliable offense than before. In Mexico City, I trust the Vikings' defense to keep this tight and give Cousins a shot to win it late.

articles.headline: Harry Kane vows to be back for 'business end of the season' after ankle surgery
articles.description: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is set to be out for several months after suffering a ligament tear in his left ankle during Bayern Munich's draw with Cologne.
articles.body:
Harry Kane is targeting the "business end of the season" after undergoing surgery on a torn ligament in his left ankle.

Bayern Munich said the operation on the injury, sustained in Friday's 1-1 draw with Cologne, was a success but the 33-year-old is expected to be out for months as a result.

Kane wrote on Instagram: "The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

"Tough times don't last, tough people do" -- my guy @edelman11 (Julian Edelman, three-time Super Bowl winner with the New England Patriots) told me this one!

"Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut."

Kane sustained the injury when he was scythed down in the area by Cologne defender Joel Schmied, who reached Michael Olise's low cross first but clattered into the Ballon d'Or winner's left leg in his follow-through at the back post.

The England captain writhed in pain and, although he gingerly got back to his feet and initially soldiered on, it was clear he could not continue and he hobbled off the field alongside two physios after treatment.

After the match Bayern confirmed Kane had torn the syndesmotic ligament and "will therefore be sidelined for the next few months."

Kane signed a new deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029 earlier this month -- reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 a week -- which made him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses.

- Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane out a 'few months' after ankle injury

- Harry Kane sets sights on Champions League, England trophy after Ballon d'Or win

- Harry Kane: England and Spain are 'the best teams in international football'

Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has bagged a scarcely believable 156 goals in 163 appearances in all competitions, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season.

He went into the international break having drawn a blank in his four previous matches for Bayern but he scored twice for England, including from the spot in their 3-2 Nations League win over Spain.

But after being forced off after 20 minutes at the Allianz Arena, replaced by Tom Bischof, Kane could now be facing a battle to be fully fit for England's two-legged quarterfinal against Norway in March.

Scott McTominay left Manchester United little over two years ago, but could he return as his Napoli contract runs down? Plus, a trio of Premier League giants are eyeing Atalanta defender Giorgio Scalvini.

The midfielder, who came through the ranks at United before making over 250 appearances for the club, is entering the final 18 months of his contract in Naples, with no progress being made on an extension. McTominay impressed upon joining Napoli in 2024, winning the Scudetto and being voted as the player of the year in his first full campaign. Now back to full fitness and impressing at the top level, Premier League clubs are lining up a move.

articles.headline: How Steelers' wide receiver corps gets big boost in Week 11
articles.description: DK Metcalf and the passing game are poised to get a lift this week with the return of Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf has never had a season like this.

A career-worst 7% drop rate. Catching a career-low 49.3% of his targets. Averaging, you guessed it, a career-low 48 yards per game and 12.3 yards per reception.

Amid the lows, though, the 28-year-old still made a handful of special plays. There was the 22-yard touchdown reception late in the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and the 32-yard catch-and-run earlier in the game. There was also the 115-yard game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 4 and the 11-catch outing in the overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6.

"This is the first time for real," Metcalf said of his struggles Thursday. "But I don't look at it as inconsistency. It's just new territory that I got to maneuver through. ... I've just got to block out the bulls--- y'all be talking about, basically."

Metcalf, who was acquired by the historically conservative organization in a blockbuster deal that included a second-round pick on the eve of 2025 free agency, was supposed to be a focal point of the offense. Instead, the mercurial wide receiver has been defined more by volatility than reliability, and this season, his 49.3% catch rate is second worst in the league out of 133 qualified players, per ESPN Research.

His teammates, though, have remained vocal in their support of him, and the coaching staff has shouldered some of the blame, saying it has to scheme up better opportunities for Metcalf.

"He's been up and down this season, and he's the first to admit that," tight end Pat Freiermuth said. "We need consistency out of him, but I've never worried about if his mind's in the right place or if he's willing to go out there and play. I think that obviously he's had some struggles, but him going out there -- and if you look at his effort on the run game or just downfield blocking, he doesn't let his situation impact his ability to get other guys open.

"That's something that you can appreciate as a teammate and as a guy, it tells a lot about his character, but we're with him till the end. He's going to get this figured out. We've got a lot of trust in DK and a lot of belief in him."

Compounding Metcalf's struggles this season has been the rash of wide receiver injuries.

But this week, Metcalf and the passing game, which averaged just 158.7 yards in the past three games, are poised to get a boost with the return of receivers Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. Though neither has been officially activated from injured reserve, each is listed as questionable for Sunday's game in Philadelphia (1 p.m. ET, CBS) after fully participating in practices Thursday and Friday.

"Instead of having four receivers up, we'll probably have five or six," Metcalf said of the pair's impact. "So I mean a lot more rotation, a lot of fresh bodies. Just watching them out there at practice these past couple days, they look fresh, they look ready to go to me."

articles.headline: Why Amarius Mims is an underrated key to Bengals' success
articles.description: Joe Burrow is on an MVP trajectory, and a big reason is his OL, led by Amarius Mims.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- One plane ride was all it took for Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Amarius Mims to realize enough was enough.

In last year's Week 4 loss to the Denver Broncos, Mims turned in a performance that made his stomach turn -- seven pressures and 1.5 sacks allowed, according to Next Gen Stats, in a humbling 28-3 blowout.

Mims watched the tape. A decision was made. He was never going to play that poorly again.

Over a year later, Mims has more than lived up to his word. Through the first half of this season, Mims has developed into not only one of Cincinnati's best players but arguably the best right tackle in the NFL.

His performance, along with that of the rest of the offensive line, has helped turn the Bengals' passing attack into the best in the NFL. Entering Monday's game against the Washington Commanders (8:15 p.m., ET, ESPN), Cincinnati leads the league in passing yards per game (298.9). And as much as the team's big stars have contributed to that total, Mims also has been a big reason for that success.

"It's crazy how my game has evolved, man," he said this week. "It's been light-years different. I'm not nowhere near the same guy I was when I first came in this building."

The advanced metrics on Mims' play have been astounding. Per Next Gen Stats, Mims is second among all offensive tackles in one-on-one pass blocking rate. This season, he has been on an island on 87.6% of his total pass blocks. And yet, his pressure rate is the lowest among all tackles at 3.3%.

For the third-year player out of Georgia, the growth stems from one hard game in Denver.

After that loss to the Broncos, he told himself he could never again put that kind of performance on tape. And in a moment of deep self-reflection, Mims watched film from the best offensive tackles in the game to see what they did well.

He also understood just how much he meant to the Bengals.

"I just flipped into another mode of like, 'Hey man, this team needs me to be a big part of this offense,' and just realizing it's time for me to flip that switch and just turn into the guy I know I can be," Mims said.

That is exactly what has happened this season, for both Mims and the entire offensive line. Mims and left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. are both ranked among the top 20 players in pass block win rate as offensive tackles. As a team, Cincinnati is ranked 19th in that category.

While those might not seem like gaudy numbers, it's worth putting them into the proper context.

No team in the NFL relies on pass blocking more than the Bengals. Cincinnati leads the NFL in designed pass play percentage (67.1%) and has the league's fewest rush attempts.

Not only does that mean the offensive line is playing on its heels for most of the game, but defensive lines are also using more pass rush strategies than they would in typical situations.

articles.headline: Giants' Abdul Carter on lack of sacks: 'I've got to do more'
articles.description: On the surface, the lack of sacks and hard numbers seem insufficient, but dig deeper and it's a different story.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The traditional numbers say one thing on New York Giants edge rusher Abdul Carter. The advanced metrics say another. It has put Carter under the microscope about whether he's actually doing enough with the immense talent at his disposal.

Carter, the No. 3 overall pick out of Penn State in the 2025 NFL draft, has two sacks, three tackles for loss and eight quarterback hits this season. That ranks him tied for 99th, 156th and tied for 55th in those categories, respectively. Not exactly impressive.   

"At the end of the day, I've got to do more, especially to get more sacks, get more production," Carter said. "But at the same time, as long as my main goal is focusing on winning."

On the surface, the lack of sacks and hard numbers seems insufficient. But dig deeper and a different story gets revealed. Carter has a 29.0% pass rush win rate, 16 forced incompletions, two interceptions created and 17 quick pressures (pressures in under 2.5 seconds). That ranks him second, first, tied for sixth and tied for eighth in those categories, respectively.

The advanced metrics depict a player making a significant impact, much like the coaches' tape.  

"I don't go through all those stats and try to dig out every little metric on every guy. We get a general accounting of it," coach John Harbaugh said. "I definitely look at the team stats. But I'm looking at the tape. Myself, I'm grading every single guy. Plus, every coach is grading their position all the time. And he's grading out really well on my sheet, I can tell you that, and the coaches' sheet. He's a disruptive guy. I promise you they're accounting for him. And the sacks are just going to come."

Carter is getting double-teamed on a team-high 41% of opposing quarterback dropbacks. That indicates a level of respect.

But somewhere there seems to be a disconnect between the pressures/disruptive plays and sacks.

"I'm trying to figure that out," Carter said.

It doesn't help that opposing quarterbacks are getting the ball out in 2.70 seconds before the pass. Only the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have seen quarterbacks get the ball out quicker. The Giants also aren't known to have one of the better interior pass rushing groups.

So there aren't a lot of freebies for Carter and the edge rushing group. Fellow outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux is still looking for his first sack of the season.

The sacks are the most glaring omission from Carter's résumé. That's where pass rushers make their name and money. Carter has just six sacks in 26 games over his first two seasons.

It's not lost on the 23-year-old edge rusher. He's seen the critiques. Just the other day, he warned on social media that he's heard the noise and to watch out Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Clearly, he's noticed the critics. And he's not backing down from the critiques.

articles.headline: Luka Doncic scores 25, Lakers barely hold off Kings 106-104 on LaVine's miss at the buzzer
articles.description: — Luka Doncic had 25 points and eight assists, Quentin Grimes hit a tiebreaking 3-pointer with 57 seconds to play, and the Los Angeles Lakers rallied in the fourth quarter for their 10th win in 11 games, 106-104 over the Sacramento Kings on Friday night.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid expected to sign Como's Nico Paz next summer
articles.description: Real Madrid are looking to boost their attack by signing Como and Argentina international Nico Paz. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：レアル・マドリード、来夏にコモのニコ・パス獲得の見込み
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードは、コモに所属するアルゼンチン代表のニコ・パスを獲得することで攻撃陣の強化を図っています。移籍情報の最新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
Real Madrid are expected to trigger the €80 million release clause in Nico Paz's contract at Como next summer, while Athletic Club winger Nico Williams is back on the radar of Arsenal, among a host of others. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are expected to trigger the €80m release clause in Nico Paz's contract at Como, following another impressive campaign in Italy. Mundo Deportivo claims that Los Blancos have until next summer to activate the clause after recent uncertainty over his future. The 22-year-old playmaker first joined Como for €6m in 2024, but a restructured €60 million deal was reached last summer that increased his release clause. Paz has scored six goals and assisted eight in 14 appearances across all competitions, giving Real Madrid a huge decision to make over his future in the coming months.

- Arsenal have reignited their interest in Athletic Club winger Nico Williams, reports TEAMtalk. The Gunners have been heavily linked with the Spain World Cup winner in the past, but after he signed a new 10-year contract extension last summer, the prospects of a deal seemingly diminished, even with a €100m exit clause inserted in the agreement. Williams is now open to a move, while Arsenal are considering options for their left flank. Real Madrid's Endrick, RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa, Brentford's Kevin Schade and Atlético Madrid forward Álex Baena are others being considered by the Premier League champions.

- Alejandro Balde continues to be linked with an exit from Barcelona, with his representatives exploring potential destinations for the left back this winter. Marca reports that the 23-year-old could make a move, with the Blaugrana keen to secure a permanent transfer rather than a loan. Any deal could be placed at roughly €40m, with Manchester United and Liverpool regularly linked.

- Aston Villa striker Tammy Abraham has emerged as an option for Valencia, according to Matteo Moretto, with contact already made. The 29-year-old has started just once under Unai Emery this campaign, which came in the EFL Cup. With a potential exit on the cards, Valencia have asked about a loan in January, with part of his salary covered.

- Napoli will let star midfielder Kevin De Bruyne leave the club in the January transfer window, if an offer of €7m arrives. Gazzetta dello Sport reports that the 35-year-old is wanted by PSV Eindhoven, which would move him closer to his native Belgium. Napoli chiefs are not keen on his exit, but will accept a move if any cost is recouped during the final six months of his contract.

Other rumors

- Chelsea have made an approach for Real Betis youngster José Antonio Morante, 19, after a breakout start to the campaign. The winger is also being tracked by Manchester City and Manchester United. (TEAMtalk)

articles.headline: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane out a 'few months' after ankle injury
articles.description: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is set to be out for several months after suffering a ligament tear in his left ankle during Bayern Munich's draw with Cologne.
articles.headlineJa: バロンドール受賞者のハリー・ケイン、足首の負傷で「数ヶ月」離脱へ
articles.descriptionJa: バロンドール受賞者のハリー・ケインが、バイエルン・ミュンヘン対ケルンの引き分け試合中に左足首の靭帯断裂を負い、数ヶ月の間離脱することが決まった。
articles.body:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is set to be sidelined for several months after suffering a ligament tear in his left ankle in the first half of Bayern Munich's draw at home to FC Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday.

Kane was hurt while attempting to get on the end of a deflected Olise cross in front of goal, when Cologne defender Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane's left leg in his follow through.

Bayern subsequently confirmed that Kane had been diagnosed with a ligament tear following an examination, adding that the England international would be out "for the next few months."

Bayer sporting director Max Eberl said they expected Kane to miss around three months.

Kane immediately clutched his lower leg after the injury and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.

The 33-year-old gestured to the sideline, sunk to the turf and then received treatment on his ankle before making way for Tom Bischof in the 20th minute, limping off the field alongside two physios.

Kane last month was announced as the men's Ballon d'Or winner after a prolific year with Bayern and England. He is Bayern's first winner of the prestigious award in 45 years and the first English winner in 25 years.

His injury means he is almost certain to miss Bayern's remaining four games in the Champions League league phase and could be in jeopardy for the start of the knockout phase, which begins in February, if Bayern progress.

England will hope that Kane has returned in time for their UEFA Nations League quarterfinal with Norway at the end of March.

Cologne were leading 1-0 at the time of Kane's injury through a 12th-minute goal from Mikey Moore before Nathaniel Brown equalized in the 37th minute.

However, Michael Olise added to Bayern's injury woes as he was substituted at the start of the second half, having hobbled off just before the break following a collision with Tom Krauss.

Olise later left the stadium on crutches, though coach Vincent Kompany said that was a precautionary measure. Bayern said that Olise had a bruised forefoot and would receive treatment in the coming days.

Any prolonged absence for Kane and Olise would be a major blow to Bayern. The pair account for 22 for Bayern's 54 goals (41%) this season.

Despite dominating possession against Cologne, Bayern had only one shot on goal over the 90 minutes as they failed to find a winner. It was the first time Bayern Munich had just one shot on target in a Bundesliga home game since at least 2004-05.

The game was Bayern's first since the November international break, in which Kane scored in England's Nations League wins over Spain and Croatia and became England's record appearance maker.

Bayern, who had Kompany back on the sidelines and with his left arm in a sling after illness, are now one point clear of Borussia Dortmund at the top of the Bundesliga ahead of Dortmund's visit to Borussia Mön
